text: If you can hold a coffee, you can close this bag.
POV: you're heading out the door. Coffee in one hand, keys in the other, and your bag is still hanging open. You're already a little late.
So you don't put anything down. Your fingers find the clasp, one press, and it snaps shut. That's the whole trick.
Then the strap. Lengthen it, slip it over your head, and the bag sits at your hip as a crossbody, out of the way of the coffee.
Your phone, your wallet and your keys already have their own spots inside, so nothing rattles around at the bottom while you walk.
At the corner your phone buzzes. Open the flap, the phone is right there in its spot, and one press shuts the bag again.
Down the street, coffee still full, your phone in the other hand, and the bag shut the whole way to the car.

Car, cafe, errands, dinner: watch what you never have to dig for.
Morning, the car. The bag rides on the seat beside you with the flap shut. When you park, you open it, and your keys are exactly where you put them.
Mid-morning, the cafe queue. Open the flap, and your phone, wallet and keys each have their own spot inside. No digging at the counter while people wait behind you.
Afternoon, the errands. Lengthen the strap and wear it crossbody, so both your hands are open for the shopping bags and the doors. The bag just stays at your hip.
Evening, dinner. Shorten the strap again and it's a handbag on the table, shut with one press of the clasp. It looks like you planned the whole day around it.
Four places, one bag, and not once did you turn it upside down to find something. Your keys, your phone and your wallet were waiting in their spots all day.
